omnis, omne

adjective, third declension, in the singular

Every one of a kind, without exception; “not every” is nōn omnis. In the plural it is “all” (see all).

Other words

  • quisque, quaeque, quodque — every (one in a series): every fifth, all the best

    pronoun and adjective, after the superlative or the ordinal it goes with · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 67: veterrima quaeque; Cic. Verr. 2.2.139: quīntō quōque annō, every fifth year (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rab. Post. 34: tertiō quōque verbō, at every other word (Lewis & Short)

    With a superlative, “all the …, every …”: optimus quisque, all the best people; doctissimus quisque, every learned man (Lewis & Short). With an ordinal, every second, third …, counted the Roman way, both ends included: tertiō quōque verbō, “at every other word”. With a word of time, “each”: quōque diē (Cic. Sen. 38). For “each” on its own, see each.

Examples

  • ut enim nōn omne vīnum, sīc nōn omnis nātūra vetustāte coacēscit

    for as not every wine turns sour with age, so not every nature doesCic. Sen. 65

  • omnem crēde diem tibi dīlūxisse suprēmum; grāta superveniet quae nōn spērābitur hōra

    believe that every day that dawns is your last: the hour you did not hope for will come as a welcome giftHor. Ep. 1.4.13–14

  • Nōn omnī eundem calceum indūcēs pedī.

    You won’t put the same shoe on every foot.Ps.-Publil. N 33

  • veterrima quaeque, ut ea vīna quae vetustātem ferunt, esse dēbet suāvissima

    every friendship, the older it is, should be the sweeter, like wines that keepCic. Amic. 67

  • quid quōque diē dīxerim, audierim, ēgerim, commemorō vesperī

    every evening I go over what I said, heard and did that dayCic. Sen. 38

See also all, each, everyone, every week, every year, every night.

SourcesLewis & Short: omnis · Lewis & Short: quisque

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-cicero-philosophica, loci-horatius, loci-publilius), checked against the editions named there.

Publilius is cited as the loci collection numbers him, by position under each initial letter in the Latin Library text; from N onwards that numbering differs from Meyer’s. “Ps.-Publil.” marks lines from the later collections printed with him.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
